query:
At Reference #1, Toronto Hydro filed a UMS Unit Costs Benchmarking Study. At Reference #2,
Toronto Hydro filed an updated UMS Unit Costs Benchmarking Study dated October 2023.
a) Please explain why unit costs for OH Switch Replacement and Switchgear Replacement
were included in the study but not included in the October 2023 UMS Study.
b) Please provide the unit costs for OH Switch Replacement and Switchgear Replacement if
calculated as part of UMS’ work for the October 2023 study but not included in the report.
c) Please provide the drivers for the increase in unit costs in the October 2023 UMS study
compared to the UMS Study for the following asset categories: UG Cable,
Pole Top Transformers, Padmount/UG Transformer, Network Transformer Replacement
and Breaker.
d) Please explain the basis for adding Cable Chambers to the asset category in the October
2023 UMS Study.
e) There were 17 electric utilities in the Peer Group Panel in the study and only
12 electric utilities in the October 2023 UMS study. Please explain and discuss any impact
on the results.
f) On of the UMS report in , UMS provides Table II-1 that shows the Fully
Normalized Benchmark Comparisons. Please provide the same table using the data in the
October 2023 UMS Study.
g) On of the UMS report in , UMS provides Table C-2 which shows the
% of Labour and Non-Labour costs. Please provide the same table using the data in the
October 2023 UMS Study.
answer:
**Summary:** The filings available to me contain only the October 2023 UMS study. They do not contain the earlier UMS study (Reference #1), and they do not contain Toronto Hydro's interrogatory response. So I can't answer (a) through (e) from the record. I can partly answer (f). I can't answer (g) as framed, because the October 2023 study has no labour/non-labour table.

**What the October 2023 study covers.** It benchmarks seven asset categories: Wood Poles, UG Cable, Pole Top Transformers, Padmount/UG Transformers, Network Transformers/Protectors, Breakers and Cable Chambers/Manholes. It also covers five maintenance programs [cite:rds-823236:381]. OH Switch Replacement and Switchgear Replacement are not among them. I searched for them in the filings and found only capital-plan discussion of those programs, not unit-cost benchmarks.

**a) and b) Why the two switch and switchgear unit costs were dropped, and what they were.** The record does not say. It has no explanation of why they were omitted, and no unit costs for them calculated by UMS.

**c) Drivers of the unit-cost increases.** I can't answer this because the earlier study's figures aren't in the record. The October study's own figures, for reference, are these 2020–2022 three-year averages [cite:rds-823236:410]:

| Asset category | THESL unit cost (C$) |
|---|---|
| UG Cable (per metre) | 131 |
| Pole Top Transformer | 18,691 |
| Padmount Transformer | 37,373 |
| Network Transformer | 127,649 |
| Breaker | 37,983 |

**d) Why Cable Chambers/Manholes were added.** The record gives no stated reason. The October study lists them as the seventh asset category [cite:rds-823236:381]. It also gives a THESL benchmark of $136,409 per chamber, 0.6% above the median [cite:rds-823236:388].

**e) Peer group of 17 versus 12.** The record doesn't discuss the earlier 17-utility panel or what the change did to the results. It does explain how the 12-utility panel was formed:
- Four Ontario utilities were invited. Only Elexicon Energy and London Hydro participated [cite:rds-823236:390].
- UMS approached the utilities from the 2017–2018 study. Eight of those participated, and the other nine declined [cite:rds-823236:390].
- Two utilities that declined last time accepted this time: Avista, and an anonymous Canadian utility [cite:rds-823236:390].
- That gives 12 in total, with 11 named plus the anonymous utility [cite:rds-823236:390].

This suggests the 17 refers to the 2017–2018 panel. I can't confirm that from the filings. UMS says no peer group is a perfect fit [cite:rds-823236:394].

**f) Table II-1 (fully normalized comparisons), October 2023 data.** The October study's Table II-1 is titled "Applying Conversion and Accounting Adjustments Only", so it is not a fully normalized table. UMS did not normalize for customer density or regional labour cost. It treated them qualitatively because of statistical and data challenges, and estimates that congestion and labour would be worth 5–10% in THESL's favour [cite:rds-823236:388]. I can't see the earlier study's "fully normalized" table to compare formats.

The October 2023 table, in C$ [cite:rds-823236:388]:

| Category | Unit | THESL | Peer median | % from median |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wood Pole | each | 8,317 | 8,181 | +1.7% |
| UG Cable (XLPE) | per m | 131 | 131 | 0.0% |
| Pole Top Transformer | each | 18,691 | 18,423 | +1.5% |
| Padmount/UG Transformer | each | 37,373 | 37,008 | +1.0% |
| Network Transformer/Protector | each | 127,649 | 130,690 | −2.3% |
| Breaker | each | 37,983 | 40,772 | −6.7% |
| Cable Chambers/Manholes | each | 136,409 | 135,571 | +0.6% |
| Vegetation Management | per line km | 2,175 | 2,139 | +1.7% |
| Pole Test and Treat | each | 17 | 19 | −10.1% |
| Overhead Line Patrol | per line km | 23 | 26 | −12.2% |
| Substation Maintenance | MVA | 1,712 | 1,681 | +1.9% |
| Building Vault Inspection | each | 258 | 268 | −3.9% |

Table C-3 in Appendix C [cite:rds-823236:410] shows the same THESL results. It differs slightly in two medians: Padmount at 37,008 and Cable Chambers at 135,579, against 135,571 in Table II-1. The Table C-3 text is inconsistent with itself in one way: it shows Cable Chambers at 135,579 in one place and 135,571 in the summary [cite:rds-823236:388]. The difference is immaterial.

**g) Table C-2 (labour and non-labour share).** In the October study, Table C-2 is "Raw Comparison (Metric and Canadian Dollar Conversion)". It shows unit costs by utility, not labour/non-labour percentages [cite:rds-823236:410]. I found no table in the October study giving percent labour versus non-labour. The study's survey form did ask peers for the percent of cost attributable to labour [cite:rds-823236:429]. The results are not published in the report. Appendix C notes the peer group is masked for confidentiality [cite:rds-823236:409].

**Next step.** Parts (a) to (e) and (g) would need to come from Toronto Hydro or UMS directly. They would need to supply the earlier study, UMS's workpapers, and the labour-share survey data.

judge.rationale: The candidate gives no answer for (a), (c), (d) and (g), which leaves out the reference's reasons for excluding switches and switchgear, the cost drivers (inflation, supply chain, COVID), the reasons for adding cable chambers, and the labour-share table. For (f) it supplies the conversion-only table, whose medians differ from the reference's fully normalized table, though it flags that difference. It overlaps with the reference only partly on (e), where utilities declined to participate, and on (b), where no unit costs exist.
